Boston College Eagles.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide directly. The guide records that Bill O'Brien has spent much of his career with quarterbacks, and that he went 7-6 in year one at Boston College before falling to 2-10.
Boston College Eagles.oc: Bill O'Brien himself — the guide records him serving as his own coordinator.
Boston College Eagles.dc: Ted Roof, a longtime friend of O'Brien's, semi-retired after being dismissed by UCF in October 2024.
Boston College Eagles.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide records O'Brien taking the job himself.
Boston College Eagles.dc_status: New — the guide records the Ted Roof hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Boston College Eagles.play_caller: Bill O'Brien on offense, explicitly — the guide notes he is serving as his own coordinator.
Boston College Eagles.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Boston College Eagles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit Roof inherits allowing over 6.5 yards per play overall and almost 470 yards per game in ACC play, with a stated goal of finding sacks after Boston College managed 17.
Boston College Eagles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Boston College Eagles.qb_development: Identified as the head coach's own specialty and his required focus. The guide says O'Brien has spent much of his career with quarterbacks and that this must be his focus, then records that he enters with virtually no Division I experience at the position — the early leader is Saginaw Valley State transfer Mason McKenzie, who had no FBS offers out of high school and faces what the guide calls a serious step up from Division II.
Boston College Eagles.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 5.
Boston College Eagles.staff_turnover: Both coordinator positions change, with the head coach absorbing one of them himself. The guide argues a 2-10 team needed an overhaul anyway — which is what has happened.
Boston College Eagles.prior_school: Georgia Tech and Duke are the shared history the guide records for O'Brien and Roof: they worked together at Georgia Tech in the 1990s and at Duke during Roof's only head coaching stint from 2003 to 2007. On the roster it records Mason McKenzie from Saginaw Valley State, Grayson Wilson having enrolled at Arkansas without playing, and Evan Dickens from Liberty.
Boston College Eagles.portal_recruiting: Addressed as necessity. The guide records almost none of last season's skill production retained — the top three receivers and the top two rushers are gone — with Liberty transfer Evan Dickens, who ran for 1,339 yards there, and sophomore Bo MacCormack expected to help.
Boston College Eagles.vsin_assessment: Blunt on the hire and on the record. The guide does not soften Ted Roof's: he went 6-45 with Duke, which it says is probably why he has been a coordinator and position coach since, and he was semi-retired after being dismissed by UCF in October 2024. On the head coach it states the stakes directly — without a bounce back this could be O'Brien's last season.
Boston College Eagles.strengths: A head coach whose career specialty is the position the guide says he must fix, a clean slate on defense the guide implies is no loss, and a portal back who ran for 1,339 yards at Liberty.
Boston College Eagles.concerns: A 2-10 season with a defense ranked 132nd nationally in yards per play allowed, a quarterback room with virtually no Division I experience led by a Division II transfer, a defensive coordinator whose only head-coaching record was 6-45 and who was semi-retired, and almost no returning skill production.
Boston College Eagles.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

California Golden Bears.previous_hc_experience: None. The Coaching Carousel records that this is Tosh Lupoi's first crack at being a head coach, and sets out the lineage instead: his college coaching career has been under Jeff Tedford, Steve Sarkisian, Nick Saban and Dan Lanning, plus three seasons in the NFL under Freddie Kitchens, Dan Quinn and Urban Meyer.
California Golden Bears.oc: Jordan Somerville, with former NFL receiver Ike Hilliard also on the offensive staff. The guide records that Cal has co-coordinators on both sides.
California Golden Bears.dc: Michael Hutchings, 31, previously at Bowling Green and Western Kentucky and then three seasons coaching Vikings defensive backs. The guide records co-coordinators on this side too.
California Golden Bears.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
California Golden Bears.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
California Golden Bears.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide records co-coordinators on both sides and leaves open whether everyone can work in harmony and raise the programme's ceiling.
California Golden Bears.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide notes a new scheme is among the obstacles facing the returning quarterback.
California Golden Bears.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide uses Lupoi's Oregon defense as the benchmark — tied for 26th nationally with 21 takeaways in 15 games and 30 sacks — against Cal's 21 sacks and 13 takeaways.
California Golden Bears.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
California Golden Bears.qb_development: Not addressed as a coaching record. The guide records Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele throwing for over 3,400 yards with an 18-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio and 64.2% completions as a true freshman, sets out the obstacles of a new scheme and new receivers, and concludes he could have a monster season.
California Golden Bears.continuity: Broken on the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 6.
California Golden Bears.staff_turnover: Complete at the top, with co-coordinator structures installed on both sides of the ball.
California Golden Bears.prior_school: Cal itself — the guide records Lupoi as a Walnut Creek native who played there from 2000 to 2005 and was the programme's defensive line coach from 2008 to 2011. Oregon is the other thread: the guide notes Somerville's single year as an Oregon offensive assistant in 2022 was enough for Lupoi to want him again, and that Lupoi and Hutchings barely overlapped there. On the roster it records Chase Henderson from Ohio and Ian Strong from Rutgers.
California Golden Bears.portal_recruiting: Addressed as replacement of departed production — Jacob De Jesus and Trond Grizzell took 163 catches and over 1,800 yards elsewhere, with Henderson and Strong arriving.
California Golden Bears.vsin_assessment: The bloodline argument, and its limits. The Coaching Carousel says Lupoi's career got it thinking about racehorses and bloodlines, lists his mentors, and grants there is a ton of coaching experience in that list which the 44-year-old had to pick up a lot from — then states the counter directly: even well-bred horses don't always work out, and Lupoi, who follows another man with a lot of good mentors in Justin Wilcox, is another defensive-minded coach at a place that badly needs an injection of offense. The team pages make the same point with a fact: Cal had No. 1 overall pick and national champion Fernando Mendoza for two seasons and went 6-7 both times, crediting Wilcox's defenses and blaming an offense that never got going.
California Golden Bears.strengths: A head coach with an unusually deep coaching lineage returning to his alma mater, a returning quarterback the guide says could have a monster season, considerable starting experience on the offensive line, a former NFL receiver on the offensive staff, and two productive portal receivers.
California Golden Bears.concerns: A first-time head coach who is defensive-minded at a programme the Carousel says badly needs an injection of offense, a 30-year-old coordinator with one year as an Oregon offensive assistant, co-coordinator structures on both sides whose harmony the guide leaves open, only three returning defensive starters, and a unit that managed 21 sacks and 13 takeaways.
California Golden Bears.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
California Golden Bears.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the hire as a career coming full circle: Lupoi's first crack at being a head coach is with his alma mater, where he was a Golden Bear from 2000-05 and the programme's defensive line coach from 2008-11. He then reaches for a metaphor — looking at Lupoi got him thinking about racehorses and bloodlines — and lists the pedigree: a college coaching career under Jeff Tedford, Steve Sarkisian, Nick Saban and Dan Lanning, plus three seasons in the NFL under Freddie Kitchens, Dan Quinn and Urban Meyer. He grants there is a ton of coaching experience in that list and that the 44-year-old had to pick up a lot of things. His counterweight is stated in the same terms: even well-bred horses don't always work out, and Lupoi, who follows another man who had a lot of good mentors in Justin Wilcox, is another defensive-minded guy at a place that badly needs an injection of offense.

Clemson Tigers.oc: Chad Morris, returning after serving as Dabo Swinney's coordinator from 2011 to 2014, replacing Garrett Riley.
Clemson Tigers.dc: Tom Allen, the former Indiana head coach, entering his second season.
Clemson Tigers.oc_status: New — the guide records Riley's departure and Morris's return, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Clemson Tigers.dc_status: Returning — Allen enters year two in the scheme, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Clemson Tigers.play_caller: Changed on offense, and the guide treats the personal dimension as the point rather than the scheme: Swinney and Riley were oil and water, and Swinney should be relieved to have Morris back.
Clemson Tigers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Clemson Tigers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Allen making the team dramatically better against the run and holding opponents to 20.5 points per game in year one.
Clemson Tigers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records Clemson running for just 3.9 yards per carry, down sharply from 5.1 the year before.
Clemson Tigers.qb_development: Addressed through a relationship rather than a technique. The guide notes Cade Klubnik had about as underwhelming a senior year as possible — a 16-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio a season after 43 total touchdowns — lists mitigating factors including that Swinney appeared at odds with Riley weekly and threw him under the bus more than once, and links that to how Klubnik's Clemson career ended. It concludes that even with Christopher Vizzina light on experience at 105 career attempts, Morris's return and a new voice in the huddle will probably help.
Clemson Tigers.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 9.
Clemson Tigers.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, and the guide describes Garrett Riley as the scapegoat.
Clemson Tigers.prior_school: Clemson itself for Morris, who held the job from 2011 to 2014. Indiana for Tom Allen. On the roster the guide records Chris Johnson arriving from SMU.
Clemson Tigers.portal_recruiting: A stated criticism of the head coach. The guide records Clemson going 7-6 while under scrutiny for being slow to adapt to the modern landscape and the portal, which has not sat well with deep-pocketed supporters, while noting Swinney's talent pipeline should make offensive improvement straightforward.
Clemson Tigers.vsin_assessment: Goodwill as the open question. The guide asks directly whether Swinney has banked enough to survive another disappointing season, given the bar at Clemson is playoff qualification and national title contention, and records the portal criticism. On the coordinator change its argument is relational — Swinney and Riley were oil and water — and its projection is that year two in Allen's scheme plus an offensive uptick could produce a Clemson team resembling the familiar version.
Clemson Tigers.strengths: A long-tenured head coach with a talent pipeline the guide says should make offensive improvement straightforward, a returning defensive coordinator credited with doing great things in year one, three of the top four tacklers back including the sack leader, a coordinator with an existing working relationship with the head coach, and an excellent receiver room.
Clemson Tigers.concerns: A 7-6 season against a playoff-contention bar, criticism for being slow to adapt to the modern landscape and the portal, a quarterback with 105 career attempts replacing a three-year starter, an open running back job after a drop from 5.1 to 3.9 yards per carry, and a secondary that was not great now losing a second-round pick.
Clemson Tigers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Duke Blue Devils.dc: Not addressed in guide. Manny Diaz is described as so accomplished defensively that the guide says the unit must step up.
Duke Blue Devils.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide refers to Brewer's year three.
Duke Blue Devils.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Duke Blue Devils.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Duke Blue Devils.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide suggests a ground-and-pound approach early given the personnel.
Duke Blue Devils.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records sacks falling from 43 to 26 and defensive numbers worsening across the board including a 1.3-yard rise in yards per play allowed that it calls hard to overlook.
Duke Blue Devils.run_pass: Addressed as a suggested direction rather than a stated policy: since Duke's offensive numbers improved while the defensive numbers worsened under Diaz, the guide suggests a ground-and-pound approach early.
Duke Blue Devils.qb_development: Addressed as a coordinator record with a caveat. The guide notes Brewer improved the group by a full yard per play and 8.3 points per game in year two, but is mostly starting from scratch in year three — for a third straight season Diaz had to find a quarterback in the portal.
Duke Blue Devils.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes for the third straight year. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 12.
Duke Blue Devils.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Duke Blue Devils.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Walker Eget from San Jose State, Jared Richardson from Penn and Javen Nicholas from Charlotte, and notes Darian Mensah moving on to Miami.
Duke Blue Devils.portal_recruiting: Framed structurally as the programme's defining problem. The guide argues success at Duke gets more impressive each season — stronger academic requirements than most in the region, and players who succeed there wanting a bigger stage elsewhere — and says portal poaching is hard for mid-tier Power Four schools to overcome annually.
Duke Blue Devils.vsin_assessment: Credit for the difficulty of the job, doubt about this particular year. The guide argues success at Duke gets more impressive each season and credits Diaz with repeatedly rebuilding at quarterback, then sets out the underlying numbers: Duke was comfortably outgained per play in ACC games and finished +10 in turnover margin, so it infers the team was fortunate Mensah played as well as he did. With Diaz so accomplished defensively, it says the unit must step up.
Duke Blue Devils.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with succeeding under structural disadvantage, both coordinators returning, a coordinator with a documented year-two improvement of a full yard per play, a 1,132-yard true freshman running back, and a big and experienced offensive line.
Duke Blue Devils.concerns: A third straight portal quarterback search, the loss of the top three pass catchers, a receiving group the guide describes thinly, sacks falling from 43 to 26 with defensive numbers worsening across the board, and only a couple of impact starters back on that side.
Duke Blue Devils.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, and the guide adds a second coaching-linked market observation: since it suggests a ground-and-pound approach early, it draws the implication that this could create value on Unders.

Florida State Seminoles.oc: Not addressed by name. The guide records a new offensive coordinator after Gus Malzahn retired.
Florida State Seminoles.dc: Tony White, entering his second season.
Florida State Seminoles.oc_status: New — the guide records Gus Malzahn's retirement and a new coordinator in his place, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Florida State Seminoles.dc_status: Returning — White enters year two, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Florida State Seminoles.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Florida State Seminoles.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Florida State Seminoles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records White cutting 6.0 points per game, 1.0 yards per carry and 0.8 yards per play year over year.
Florida State Seminoles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Florida State Seminoles.qb_development: Not addressed as a coaching record. The guide's quarterback conclusion is about resourcing rather than development: Ashton Daniels and redshirt freshman Kevin Sperry are not the quarterbacks a programme like Florida State should have — and neither, it adds, was Tommy Castellanos.
Florida State Seminoles.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback both change, and there is a new special teams coordinator. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 9.
Florida State Seminoles.staff_turnover: Framed by the guide as a substitute for a head-coaching change. Its opening argument is buyout economics: dismissing head coaches has become expensive, and where schools cannot raise the cash, assistants take the blame instead — and in Tallahassee it reads as the latter, with Mike Norvell remaining alongside a new special teams coordinator, a new offensive coordinator and a second-year defensive coordinator.
Florida State Seminoles.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Ashton Daniels having flashed at Stanford before starting only three games at Auburn, and a 133-tackle addition from Southern Miss.
Florida State Seminoles.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect.
Florida State Seminoles.vsin_assessment: A programme the guide says is held hostage by a contract. It records Norvell's buyout as still north of $50 million at season's end and questions whether a third straight season without contention or a bowl would be tolerated. On the field it asks the genuinely open question — bad luck or bad coaching — after Florida State went 0-5 on the road and 2-6 in conference play while posting +0.84 yards per play in ACC games and losing with a yardage edge to Virginia, Miami, Stanford, Clemson and NC State. Its blunt conclusion links football to finance: Norvell's buyout appears to hold the programme hostage.
Florida State Seminoles.strengths: A second-year defensive coordinator with documented year-over-year improvement across points, yards per carry and yards per play; a good defensive foundation in the sack leader, the tackles-for-loss leader and a 133-tackle portal addition; and a conference yardage margin that the guide says was better than the record.
Florida State Seminoles.concerns: A head coach the guide implies is retained by buyout economics rather than results, a new offensive coordinator after a retirement, a quarterback room the guide says is below the programme's standard, and a -5 turnover margin with only 14 takeaways in 12 games and just two of 14 forced fumbles recovered.
Florida State Seminoles.betting: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins, though the guide explicitly says this is not a bet — the vig is cost-prohibitive and Florida State projects to have a good defense.

Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.oc: George Godsey, who played quarterback at Georgia Tech from 1998 to 2001 and returns after four seasons as the Ravens' tight ends coach, replacing Buster Faulkner, who left for Florida.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.dc: Jason Semore, who spent three seasons with Charles Huff at Marshall then Southern Miss, replacing Blake Gideon, who returned to Texas.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.oc_status: New — the guide records Faulkner's departure and Godsey's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.dc_status: New — the guide records Gideon's return to Texas and Semore's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide makes a schematic prediction: expect a more ball-control offense, since Georgia Tech ranked 97th in average time of possession, with a jump likely there.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide characterises Semore by output, recording that Southern Miss's 29 takeaways ranked fourth in FBS with 23 interceptions leading the nation.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.tempo: Expected to slow — the guide predicts a more ball-control offense from a team that ranked 97th in average time of possession.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the ball-control prediction.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.personnel: Addressed indirectly through the tight end fit — the guide likes Godsey's Ravens tight ends background given two of Tech's best portal additions were tight ends.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.qb_development: Addressed as an unknown. After success with Texas A&M transfer Haynes King the staff went back to the portal for Alberto Mendoza, and the guide is candid that nobody knows what to expect from him, since Curt Cignetti rarely eased off at Indiana and he played little.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 6.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.staff_turnover: Extensive and enumerated. The guide records both coordinators leaving — Faulkner to Florida and Gideon back to Texas — plus the offensive line coach, and summarises the whole picture cumulatively: new quarterback, new feature back, an entirely new receiver room, two new but productive transfer tight ends, and new coordinators on both sides. While crediting Brent Key and noting turnover is nothing new, it calls this a lot.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.prior_school: Georgia Tech itself for Godsey, who played quarterback there. Marshall and Southern Miss under Charles Huff for Semore, and the Baltimore Ravens for Godsey's most recent job. On the roster the guide records Alberto Mendoza from Indiana and Justice Haynes from Michigan.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.portal_recruiting: Named as one of the three pillars of the guide's case. It cites what Key has done so far, the caliber of coordinators he has hired, and the programme's portal success — recording the earlier Haynes King success and the Mendoza and Haynes additions.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.vsin_assessment: Optimistic, and explicit about why. The guide says three straight losses to end the season pushed the last ten-win season further into the past but that Key came very close in his fourth full year, and finds silver linings in both coordinator hires. Its case rests on three things it names together — what Key has done so far, the caliber of coordinators he has hired, and the programme's portal success — giving more reasons for optimism than pessimism even with a projection of 6.02 wins.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with coming very close to ten wins and with a record of portal success, two coordinator hires it finds silver linings in — one a former Georgia Tech quarterback with an NFL tight ends background matching the roster, the other from a defense that ranked fourth in FBS in takeaways — and a clear schematic direction toward ball control.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.concerns: Turnover the guide itself calls a lot: new coordinators on both sides, the offensive line coach gone with three line starters, only one player with at least six receptions returning across the receiver and tight end rooms, and a portal quarterback nobody knows what to expect from.
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-adjacent market note is that Georgia Tech have covered every Georgia game under Key, though this one is back on the road.
